AXP.rationale: American Express shows solid fundamental health with consistent revenue and EPS growth (Q1 2026 revenue +9.3% YoY, EPS +17.6% YoY), strong ROE of 33%, and a premium closed-loop business model that supports durable competitive advantages. The company's focus on affluent consumers and high-spending cardholders provides resilience, with net charge-off rates of 2.3% well below peers. Valuation has compressed meaningfully from its 2025 highs, with P/E now at 19.3x versus a 25.3x peak in the window, placing it near the low end of its 365-day range. However, the stock remains fairly valued rather than clearly cheap, and there are macro headwinds including rising 10-year Treasury yields (4.45%), elevated oil prices ($92.65/bbl), and potential credit normalization risks. The 16% dividend increase and GBT stake sale provide modest positive catalysts, but no major near-term re-rating event is evident. The score reflects a quality franchise at a more reasonable but not deeply discounted valuation.
key_factors: Consistent revenue and EPS growth trajectory (Q1 2026: revenue +9.3% YoY, EPS +17.6% YoY)
Strong ROE of 33% and net margins of 26.6%
P/E compressed to 19.3x from 25.3x peak, near low end of 365-day range
Premium closed-loop business model with high cardholder spend ($150 avg transaction vs $91-94 competitors)
Net charge-off rate of 2.3% below peers like Capital One at 3.7%
16% dividend increase and GBT stake sale providing capital flexibility
Rising Treasury yields and elevated oil prices as macro headwinds
Regulatory risk on interchange fees and credit card interest rate caps

sources_cited.excerpt: average Amex transaction was $150, compared to roughly $94 for Mastercard and $91 for Visa; net charge-off rate was 2.3%
16% dividend increase and groundbreaking of new global headquarters at 2 World Trade Center
exiting its roughly 30% equity stake in Global Business Travel...about US$1.5b in proceeds and US$975m pre tax gain
